# Rosalind Penrose

## Overview

- **Age:** Forty-five years old  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>
- **Origin:** Welby  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045)</sub>

## Appearance

Rosalind is a tiny woman with thick, wavy, snow-white hair set in flattering puffs and coils. Beneath her hair, she has a remarkably bright, youthful complexion with rosy cheeks, sweet lips, dimples, and wood-brown eyes containing flecks of gold. Her voice has been described as recalling white satin, splashing water, and fairy bells, and she favors delicate dresses adorned with floral patterns.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002)_

## Personality

Rosalind possesses a playful, imaginative nature and delights in hosting pretend tea parties and engaging in whimsical amusements. Although considered odd by some for her divergence from social norms and her preference for isolation, she maintains a cheerful, unbothered attitude toward others' opinions of her. She has a confessed vanity for fine clothes and enjoys flouting conventional dietary rules in her home.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086), [v2 c22 P6](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0006), [v2 c27 P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029), [v2 c28 P19](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0019)_

## Traits

- Imaginative and playful  <sub>[v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Indifferent to rumors or public opinion  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Vain about fine clothes  <sub>[v2 c28 P19](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0019)</sub>
- Fear of the pain of losing friends who depart  <sub>[v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)</sub>

## History

Rosalind Penrose grew up in Welby, named by her father after his love for lavender sheets during his courtship of her mother. In her youth, she was considered a beauty and became betrothed to Stephen Stanhope, but the engagement suddenly ended following a disagreement, prompting Stanhope to leave for the United States. After her mother died a decade prior, Rosalind withdrew into Echo Cottage—an ancient stone house built by her English grandfather—and effectively faded from local social life. Unable to afford an adult servant, she arranged for a succession of young handmaidens from the Bowman family to live with her; because of their similar appearances, she called each of them "Belinda" in turn up through Belinda the Fourth. She later formed a close friendship with schoolmistress Nell Harcourt, frequently hosting her for tea, confectionery making, and pretend parties. Eventually, Stephen Stanhope returned, rekindled their romance, and escorted her on forest walks. They were married in an unceremonious service in the honeysuckle garden at Echo Cottage, officiated by Mr. Wace.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010), [v2 c30 P12](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0012), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030)_

## Background by volume

- Named Rosalind by her father due to his love for the fragrance of lavender  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Considered a great beauty in her youth  <sub>[v2 c22 P3](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0003)</sub>
- Was engaged to Stephen Stanhope twenty-five years ago before a quarrel separated them  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>
- Withdrew from social life at Echo Cottage following her mother's death a decade prior  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007)</sub>
- Employed a succession of young Bowman handmaidens whom she collectively referred to as Belinda  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> Each of you girls will get a cluster of lavender from me  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>

> Should we come across a newspaper piece cautioning about a treat we enjoy, we snip it out and attach it to the kitchen wall for memory's sake.  <sub>[v2 c27 P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029)</sub>

> After a bit, they merely depart from your life, leaving behind an ache that exceeds the void existing before their arrival.  <sub>[v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)</sub>

> How silly and light-headed I have to be  <sub>[v2 c28 P19](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0019)</sub>
